target_semantics.rel: relative to F_1(x) at each node
target_semantics.abs: plain absolute 5e-14 on F_1 (not F_0-scaled); its model L is log(F_1(a)/5e-14)

f0_bands.note: the paper's own x0 records (published re-count for Chebyshev, core sweep for rational) against results-second-edge; the same estimators as the F_1 side, so the bands are like-for-like

chebyshev_rate_model.statement: the Chebyshev rate is log(1/kappa) for every alpha (the paper's tail-class proposition): the branch point at zero and the band fix kappa, and a non-vanishing analytic factor moves only the constant. F_1/F_0 = g/(2 x erf(sqrt(x))) is analytic and positive on [a, a+W] for a > 0, so F_1 has F_0's Chebyshev rate at matched W/a; the free constant is C_c.

rational_rate_model.statement: F_1 = (sqrt(pi)/4) x^(-3/2) g(x) with g analytic and non-vanishing on the band; x^(-3/2) = x^(-1/2) * (1/x) and 1/x is analytic and non-vanishing for a > 0, so the exponential rational rate is the alpha = 1/2 rate: mu_{3/2}(kappa) = mu(kappa), the Groetzsch ring function. The alpha-dependence is in the constant C_r, not the rate; the sheet count of x^(3/2) is 2, not 3.
rational_rate_model.subsidiary_argument: F_1/F_0 is analytic and non-vanishing on the band; multiplying by such a factor leaves the nth-root rate unchanged, so both families inherit F_0's rates at matched W/a.
rational_rate_model.fallback_if_derivation_declined: the rational-rate prediction is not established independently; the rational counts and their slopes stand as measurements

matched_kappa.statement: the a2 edge doubles every Group A width, so W/a and kappa(W/a) are matched; the sweep's stored width text is what fixes kappa

ladder.note: the paper's free-line rule (largest residual and every second difference at most one stored coefficient, no model rate) applied to the three Group A targets; second differences carry the unequal-L spacing correction
